The four things a committee is judged on.

Transparent

Every bill carries the formula, the inputs and a step-by-step trace. A resident sees how their number was reached, not just the number.

Organized

Buildings, flats, residents, meters, tickets, tasks and bookings in one structure — so nothing lives in one person's phone.

Secure

A separate database per society, twelve roles, ninety-plus permissions — and a neighbour's flat that answers "not found", never "not allowed".

Connected

Notices, approvals and ticket updates arrive the moment they happen — and are still there when the connection drops.

Live today

Fifteen modules your society already runs on.

Not a roadmap. Every module below is built, tested and running — the screens a committee opens on the first of the month and the ones a guard opens forty times a day.

Live

Maintenance billing

Bill 300 flats in one run, on whatever cycle your society actually uses.

  • Monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly cycles aligned to the Indian financial year
  • Different templates for different towers, flat types or occupancy
  • Published bills are frozen — a rate change makes version N+1, it does not rewrite history
Live

Visual bill builder

Build the charge the way you would explain it — no formula language to learn.

  • Drag blocks: add, multiply, percentage, slab rate, round, if / otherwise
  • Preview any flat's bill before a single resident sees it
  • Amounts are computed on the server in exact decimal, never in the browser
Live

Payments & receipts

Record what came in, against which bill, and watch the outstanding figure move.

  • Part payments, advances and adjustments against a bill
  • Outstanding by flat, by building and by quarter
  • A defaulters list the committee can act on, not argue about
Live

Water & electricity meters

A meter reader walks one building and enters one number per flat.

  • Each row prefilled with last round's closing reading
  • Consumption is computed by the database, so a correction can never leave a stale figure
  • A reading below the last one is refused at the keyboard, not on the bill
Live

Complaints & SLA

Eleven categories, a ticket number nobody can duplicate, and a clock on every one.

  • Response and resolution targets set by category and priority
  • A full timeline, plus internal notes residents never see
  • Stale tickets auto-close; breached ones escalate overnight
Live

Maintenance & housekeeping

The intention and the evidence, kept apart on purpose.

  • Schedules say "the lift is serviced monthly"; tasks record what happened in March
  • Assign, start, complete, verify — a worker cannot sign off their own job
  • A skipped month stays visible instead of quietly disappearing
Live

Visitors & gate

Nobody walks in because the guard recognised them.

  • Pre-approve a guest and share a pass code that avoids 0/O and 1/I/L
  • A walk-up waits at "awaiting approval" until the flat says yes
  • A denied visitor cannot be admitted at all — that takes a fresh entry

Notices & announcements

Say it once, to exactly the people it concerns.

  • Target everyone, one tower, one wing, owners only, tenants only or staff
  • Schedule a notice now and let it appear on Saturday morning
  • Read receipts counted once per person, so "nobody told us" has an answer

Amenity booking

The party lawn, the clubhouse, the badminton court — booked without a WhatsApp argument.

Structure & residents

Buildings, blocks, floors, flats, residents and their families — set up in an afternoon.

Parking, vehicles & pets

Reports & exports

Ten reports, every one of them downloadable as CSV for the auditor.

Why NestFlow

Most society apps do the same six things. This is where NestFlow diverges.

Gate passes, notices and a maintenance bill are table stakes — every product in this market has them. The differences that matter show up on the first of the month, and in the argument that follows.

01

Billing is a formula, not a form

Nearly every society app offers a fixed set of charge heads — per square foot, per flat, a flat amount, maybe one water slab. Real societies are messier than that: a vacancy rebate, a different rate for rented flats, a tower that pays for its own lift, a slab that only applies above 10 kL.

NestFlow gives you a visual builder with add, multiply, percentage, slab, min, max, and if / otherwise, composed into a tree. If you can explain the charge in a sentence, you can build it.

No spreadsheet kept alongside "the app" for the four flats that don't fit.
02

Last quarter still adds up

When a rate changes in most systems, the rate is simply overwritten. Reopen an old bill and it either shows today's number or a stored total nobody can reproduce.

Publishing a NestFlow template freezes that version. A rate change creates version N+1, and database triggers refuse to alter a published bill's amounts. March's bill still recomputes to exactly what that resident was charged in March.

The audit at year end stops being an archaeology exercise.
03

Every bill can explain itself

The most expensive thing in a society is not the maintenance charge — it is the four hours a committee spends defending it in the WhatsApp group.

Each NestFlow bill stores its formula snapshot, its input snapshot and a step-by-step trace. A resident taps "how was this calculated?" and gets the actual working: 2,400 base, 1,230 sq ft at ₹2.40, 12.4 kL of water across two slabs.

A number invites an argument. A derivation ends one.
04

Your data is a database, not a column

The standard SaaS approach is one shared database with a society_id on every row. One missed filter in one query and a neighbouring society sees your defaulters list.

NestFlow provisions a physically separate PostgreSQL database for every society. Isolation becomes a property of how connections are routed, not of remembering a WHERE clause. No endpoint anywhere accepts a society id.

Also means your society can be backed up, exported or handed over on its own.
05

Roles that match a real household

Most apps model a flat as one owner plus one tenant. Households are not shaped like that — there is a father who pays, a spouse who books the clubhouse, a son at college, and a teenager who should be able to let a friend in but not approve a ₹6,000 bill.

NestFlow has owner, co-admin, member and child accounts inside a single flat, on top of twelve roles and ninety-plus permissions for staff and committee.

And a neighbour's flat answers "not found" — never "not allowed".
06

The database enforces the rules

Thirty families open the booking screen at 9 a.m. on Sunday. A check-then-insert written in application code passes every test and loses every Sunday.

NestFlow pushes the guarantees down: an exclusion constraint makes double-booking impossible, consumption is a generated column so a corrected reading can never leave a stale figure, and a meter reading below the last one is refused before it is saved.

Correctness you do not have to trust a developer to have remembered.

Where the established apps are still ahead

They have mature mobile apps, built-in payment collection, accounting exports and years of gate-hardware integrations. NestFlow's mobile app, online payments and ANPR gate access are on the roadmap, not in your hands today. If collecting money inside the app on day one is your deciding factor, we are not there yet — and you should hear that from us rather than find it out in month two.

Who it's for

Everyone opens the same app and sees a different one.

A guard should never see a bill. A resident should never see the society's whole vehicle register. NestFlow decides that per person, on every request.

Committee & treasurer

Bill runs, payments, defaulters, reports, notices, the whole society's structure and staff.

Resident family

Their bills, their meters, their complaints, their guests and their bookings. Owner, co-admin, member and child accounts per flat.

Security

One screen: who is at the gate, which flat they want, and whether that flat said yes. Nothing about money.

Housekeeping & maintenance

Today's tasks, the tickets assigned to them, and a completion their supervisor verifies.

Managing many societies

Provision a new society in one step — its own database, its own roles, its own branding — then lock, extend or archive it.

How it's built

Three rules the whole system is shaped around.

A society's money and a society's residents are not things to be careful with occasionally. These are enforced by the architecture, not by remembering.

RULE 01

Your society is never named in a request

No screen, link or app can ask for another society's data, because there is nowhere to put the question. Which society you belong to is decided from who you are, every single request — and your data lives in a separate PostgreSQL database from every other society's.

RULE 02

Signing in and being allowed are separate

Your identity comes from Firebase; what you may do comes from NestFlow's own tables. So removing someone from the committee takes effect on their next tap, not in an hour when a token happens to expire.

RULE 03

Money is computed on the server

The bill builder is an editor. The authority is a formula engine on the server that reads a structured tree, never a text expression — so there is no expression to escape from, and a browser cannot talk NestFlow into a different number.

Built on

PostgreSQL 17 · one database per society FastAPI · Python 3.12 React 19 · TypeScript strict Firebase Authentication Live updates over WebSocket Nightly sweeps, every one idempotent 401 tests against a real database
